triggers: a kernel on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942) risks the '2. block_n=64 silently drops half the K/V rows (correctness failure)' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942): 2. block_n=64 silently drops half the K/V rows (correctness failure)

problem.statement: Pitfalls: FlyDSL Attention Backward dQ + dK+dV on MI308X (gfx942) -- 2. block_n=64 silently drops half the K/V rows (correctness failure)

payload.attempted: Increasing block_n from 32 to 64 doubles the K/V tile size per workgroup, reducing total workgroups and loop iterations. Benchmark shows 22% TFLOPS improvement, suggesting a clear win.
payload.lesson: Always run correctness checks before trusting benchmark numbers. A kernel that silently computes half the output will appear faster while being wrong. The MFMA32x32x8 output layout fundamentally limits the N dimension to 32 rows per tile without inner tiling.

established_fact.mechanism: MFMA32x32x8 C output maps `lane_mod_32` (lane_id % 32) to the row index. With 64-wide waves, only 32 unique row positions exist. The store logic uses `k_row = n_start + lane_mod_32`, which only covers the first 32 rows of the 64-row tile. Supporting block_n=64 would require an inner n_chunk loop that processes two 32-row sub-tiles sequentially.

payload.observed: Rows 32-63 of dK and dV output are all zeros. 50% of KV rows are never computed.
payload.root_cause: MFMA32x32x8 C output maps `lane_mod_32` (lane_id % 32) to the row index. With 64-wide waves, only 32 unique row positions exist. Supporting block_n=64 would require an inner n_chunk loop that processes two 32-row sub-tiles sequentially.
